title: Quarto Quick Guide
text:
Quick guide to edit, build and deploy this website built with Quarto.

Preview Site
Preview the site locally.


Terminal

quarto preview <site-name> 
# e.g., quarto preview ytian-web



Edit Nav and Sidebars
Website navigation is defined in the _quarto.yml file in the root folder.
Edit the _quarto.yml YAML file to add or remove sidebar attributes.



Freeze Posts with Code
Render and freeze a post with freeze:true in the _metadata.yml file under the posts folder.
You can explicitly re-render it when needed.


Terminal

# render single document (always executes code)
quarto render document.qmd

# render project subdirectory (always executes code)
quarto render articles

title: QuickStart
text:
Assuming you already have the repo on your local machine.

Be sure your local repo is up-to-date with the remote repo.

Two basic commands: git pull and git push. The git pull can be divided into git fetch and git merge.
A, then a common workflow will have 4 steps:

You ALWAYS need to be sure your local repo is up-to-date with the remote repo.



Terminal

#Make sure there are no untracked files.
git status 

#Pull in all the files changed on the remote
git fetch

#Comfirm that all the files are ready to merge
git status

#A final step in pulling the remote changes into local machine
git merge

#A final "git status" to confirm everything is good to go
git status


With some modifications/changes in your working directory, it is time to inform Git about your new changes using git add -A.

#Stage all the changed or newly added files in the working directory
git add -A

#Confirm again.
git status

It’s time to git commit -m!

git commit -m "this is my commit"

#Confirm again
git status

The final git push to the remote repository.

git push

# Confirm everything is up-to-date
git status
